answer: Sybil resistance comes from binding each agent identity to a remotely verified enclave measurement (MRENCLAVE) and its hardware-rooted attestation key. MRENCLAVE identifies the approved code, while the non-exportable key proves execution on genuine silicon; copying a VM or its files cannot reproduce that proof. Creating another identity therefore requires another attested hardware instance, not merely a virtual clone. The grove of agents can share a vertex protocol and cipher suite without sharing hardware identities.
